h2: Getting NDT certified in the Northeast: what naval, nuclear and plant employers expect
html:
Getting NDT certified in the Northeast: what naval, nuclear and plant employers expect

In the Northeast, as elsewhere in the US, an NDT technician is certified by an employer, and that employer's program decides which training counts. Atlantis' online Level I and Level II courses teach SNT-TC-1A method theory, with practicals arranged with the employer.

Naval work and NAVSEA T9074. The NAVSEA publication Requirements for Nondestructive Testing Methods covers radiography, magnetic particle, penetrant, ultrasonic, eddy current and visual inspection, and is applied across naval shipyards, Forces Afloat and naval repair facilities. It requires personnel to be certified in accordance with SNT-TC-1A guidelines, recertified at least every three years (every five for examiners), and given a vision test every year. Two details matter for anyone moving between Northeast employers. First, certifications may not be transferred to another activity unless NAVSEA authorizes it, so a technician who moves between a yard and a supplier should expect to be re-examined. Second, every procedure has to be qualified by finding known discontinuities, and acceptance criteria come from the contract or ship specification, not from the NDT document. Whether a naval program will accept classroom hours from an outside course is the employer's decision, so confirm it with the employer's NDT Level III before you enroll.

Power and process plants. Western Pennsylvania's Beaver Valley Nuclear Power Station, about 34 miles from Pittsburgh, is now owned by Irving, Texas-based Vistra after the NRC approved the license transfer from Energy Harbor in 2023. Nuclear in-service inspection runs under ASME Section XI with its own personnel qualification layer, so an SNT-TC-1A certificate is where a nuclear career starts, not where it ends. Refineries, chemical plants, utilities and fabrication shops across New York, New Jersey and Pennsylvania hire against SNT-TC-1A written practices, usually starting with UT thickness, MT, PT and VT.

Radiography trainees. Connecticut, Maine, Massachusetts, New Hampshire, Vermont, Rhode Island, New York, New Jersey, Pennsylvania and Maryland are all NRC Agreement States, so radioactive material licensing and radiographer requirements are set by each state's radiation program. That radiation-safety qualification is separate from RT method training and from the employer's SNT-TC-1A certification.

Where to start, depending on your situation:

  • New to NDT: Level I training, then Level II training, both through online NDT training that you can start at any time
  • Logging experience for certification: the SNT-TC-1A hours planner keeps classroom and on-the-job hours in a form an employer can verify
  • Practicing before the practical: Practical NDT simulators and free practice tests
  • Working toward Level III: ASNT NDT Level III exam preparation
  • Employers building a program: SNT-TC-1A training program setup, and outsourced ASNT NDT Level III support for the written practice and examinations

City detail for the region's main markets is on the Boston, Pittsburgh and Groton training pages. To plan training for one technician or a crew, tell us the methods, levels and which certification scheme your employer works to through the Northeast NDT training enquiry.
